name: Dirty Yellow
lede: Dirty Yellow is a dense, greenish yellow named by the 2010 xkcd color survey, and one of the rarest colors we can match in painting.

sections.title: A survey name for a vivid, murky yellow
sections.body:
The only recorded source for Dirty Yellow is the xkcd survey of 2010, following the plain modifier grammar *dirty* plus [[yellow]] [1]. At hex #CDC50A it measures lightness 78 and chroma 79 in LCH, close in strength to the nearest ISCC-NBS block, a vivid greenish yellow only 1.1 units off, despite the word *dirty* in its name [1].

Its closest named neighbor is [[citronelle|Citronelle]], 4.1 units away and lighter, also an xkcd-era name [2]. [[citrine|Citrine]] sits 4.4 units off, lighter still [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This match appears in 0.02% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (5 paintings, as photographed); the within-painting lens narrows that to 6 [3]. In our archive it is rarer than 73% of the named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent across its 6 appearances by lightness rank within the painting [3]. The earliest match dates to 1700, 310 years before the name's 2010 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment or dye [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
